jurisdiction.name: Brazil
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Brazil has no general AI law yet: the AI framework bill PL 2338/2023 passed the Senate in December 2024 and, as of October 2026, awaits the rapporteur's report in a Câmara special committee. AI-relevant federal law includes the LGPD, whose article 20 gives a right to review of automated decisions, the 2025 ECA Digital and its 2026 decree with duties for AI tools and conversational agents used by children, criminal laws on AI-generated sexual content and AI-enabled violence against women, and a May 2026 decree barring internet providers from using AI to generate non-consensual intimate content. Policy rests on the Brazilian AI Strategy (EBIA, 2021) and the Brazilian AI Plan 2024-2028 (PBIA), with the Ministry of Management's AI strategy, AI governance policy and guides for public servants, and CNJ Resolution 615/2025 governing AI in the courts. Regulators are active: the data protection agency (renamed Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados in 2026) suspended Meta's AI training in 2024, runs an AI sandbox and made AI an enforcement priority; the electoral court requires labelling of AI content and bans deepfakes in campaigns; and CVM, ANVISA, ANATEL and the central bank have AI-related rules. States including Paraná, Santa Catarina, Goiás, Ceará and Pernambuco have AI laws, and the cities of São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Belo Horizonte, Curitiba and Recife have AI laws, decrees or staff rules.

Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos (Secretaria de Governo Digital)

narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 11 October 2026, covering federal laws, decrees and bills, federal ministries, the courts' national council, federal regulators, nine priority states plus Ceará, and the cities of São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Recife, Belo Horizonte, Curitiba and Porto Alegre. Searches were made in Portuguese and English. Some official websites could not be read automatically, including the electoral court, the Rio de Janeiro state assembly's legislation database, the Rio city council and the platform hosting the full Brazilian AI Plan; records from those sites are marked as located but not fully read, or held as pending. Bills, including the national AI bill PL 2338/2023, are listed as pending rather than as instruments. Pending: the national AI bill, Rio de Janeiro state's AI and facial-recognition law, the G20 Maceió and BRICS AI declarations, AI rules of other ministries and of the remaining states, and Salvador and Fortaleza.

instruments.official_title: Estratégia Brasileira de Inteligência Artificial (EBIA) — Portaria GM nº 4.617, de 6 de abril de 2021
instruments.english_title: Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Strategy (EBIA) — MCTI Ordinance No. 4,617 of 6 April 2021
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovações (Gabinete do Ministro; Minister Marcos Cesar Pontes)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação
instruments.current_status: Instituted by Portaria GM nº 4.617 of 6 April 2021, in force on publication (DOU 9 April 2021, Seção 1, p. 21); republished with its Annex in DOU of 12 April 2021 (Seção 1, p. 30) because the first publication omitted the Annex. The Annex (the strategy text) was replaced in full by Portaria MCTI nº 4.979 of 13 July 2021 (DOU 15 July 2021, Seção 1, p. 16), which is the current text. No official act states that the EBIA was replaced by the Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial 2024-2028; MCTI still presents it as current (page updated 13 January 2026) and Portaria MGI nº 3.485/2026 cites Portaria nº 4.617 as a legal basis. A strategy, not law.
instruments.scope: Federal government (União); orients federal AI policy
instruments.summary: Brazil's first national AI strategy, instituted by MCTI ordinance to guide state action on AI research, development and innovation and its conscious and ethical use. The strategy (as replaced by Portaria MCTI nº 4.979/2021) sets out nine thematic axes — three transversal (legislation, regulation and ethical use; AI governance; international aspects) and six vertical (education, workforce and training, R&D and entrepreneurship, application in productive sectors, application in government, public security) — each with a diagnosis and strategic actions. The ordinance charges MCTI with creating governance bodies to prioritise, monitor and update the actions, inviting public, private and academic partners, and publishing evaluation reports.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Brazilian federal instrument shaping AI governance (strategy, ethics, government-governance).

instruments.summary: Ministry-level AI strategy that orients how MGI builds the institutional capacity for responsible, safe and ethical use of AI, aligned with the Federal Digital Government Strategy. It sets a vision, six principles (human rights and equity; transparency, explainability and auditability; security and non-maleficence; privacy and data protection; effective human oversight and accountability; socio-environmental sustainability), pillars such as human engagement, optimisation and automation and insight generation, objectives and competencies, with appendices on expected benefits, suggested metrics and risks. It was drafted by an AI working group (GT-IA) created by Resolução CGDSI/MGI nº 6 of 5 December 2024 and coordinated by the Secretaria de Governo Digital.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Brazilian federal instrument shaping AI governance (public-sector, strategy, ethics).

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 13.709, de 14 de agosto de 2018
instruments.english_title: Law No. 13,709 of 14 August 2018 – General Personal Data Protection Law (LGPD)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned 14 August 2018 and published in the DOU of 15 August 2018 (partially republished the same day in an extra edition). Art. 65 (as amended by Lei nº 13.853/2019 and Lei nº 14.010/2020) stages commencement: ANPD provisions (arts. 55-A to 55-L, 58-A, 58-B) on 28 December 2018; sanctions (arts. 52-54) on 1 August 2021; all other articles 24 months after publication. The deferral to 3 May 2021 in Medida Provisória nº 959/2020 was not kept when that MP was converted into Lei nº 14.058 (17 September 2020, DOU 18 September 2020), so the general provisions apply from 18 September 2020; that date is not written in the Planalto text and is recorded from the conversion record. Latest amendment shown in the compiled text: Lei nº 15.352, de 25 de fevereiro de 2026 (ANPD renamed Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados).
instruments.summary: Brazil's general data protection law: it governs any processing of personal data by public or private persons, sets the legal bases, data-subject rights, controller/processor duties, international transfer rules and administrative sanctions, and is enforced by the ANPD. Art. 20 gives data subjects the right to request review of decisions taken solely on the basis of automated processing of personal data that affect their interests (including profiling for personal, professional, consumer or credit purposes), requires controllers to give clear information on the criteria and procedures of the automated decision, and allows the ANPD to audit for discriminatory aspects where trade secrecy is invoked.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing personal data used to train and deploy AI; art. 20 is Brazil's in-force rule on review of solely automated decisions.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 13.853, de 8 de julho de 2019
instruments.english_title: Law No. 13,853 of 8 July 2019 – amends the LGPD and creates the National Data Protection Authority (conversion of Provisional Measure No. 869/2018)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned 8 July 2019 (conversion of Medida Provisória nº 869, de 27 de dezembro de 2018) and published in the DOU of 9 July 2019; art. 4 provides entry into force on publication. Parts of the presidential veto were later overridden and promulgated (linked on the Planalto page); the proposed art. 20 § 3 remains vetoed. Its amendments are consolidated into the LGPD; ANPD provisions were later amended by Lei nº 14.460/2022 and Lei nº 15.352/2026.
instruments.summary: Amending law that gave the LGPD its short name, created the Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) and the Conselho Nacional de Proteção de Dados Pessoais e da Privacidade, and rewrote art. 65 to stage the LGPD's commencement. It rewrote LGPD art. 20 so that data subjects may request review of solely automated decisions without the earlier requirement that the review be carried out by a natural person.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Set the current wording of LGPD art. 20 on automated decisions and created the data protection authority that supervises AI-related processing.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 14.460, de 25 de outubro de 2022
instruments.english_title: Law No. 14,460 of 25 October 2022 – transforms the National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) into a special-nature autarchy (conversion of Provisional Measure No. 1,124/2022)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated by the President of the Congress (Mesa do Congresso Nacional) on 25 October 2022 as the conversion of Medida Provisória nº 1.124/2022; published in the DOU of 26 October 2022; art. 10 provides entry into force on publication. ANPD provisions later amended again by Lei nº 15.352/2026.
instruments.summary: Transforms the ANPD from a body of the Presidency into an autarchy of special nature with technical and decision-making autonomy, own assets and seat in Brasília, keeping its structure and competences. It amends the LGPD's ANPD chapter and Lei nº 13.844/2019 and revokes the LGPD provisions inserted by Lei nº 13.853/2019 on the authority's transitional legal nature (art. 55-A §§ 1-3), art. 55-B and art. 55-C, V.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Gave the data protection authority, which supervises automated decisions and AI-related processing, independent autarchy status.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 15.352, de 25 de fevereiro de 2026
instruments.english_title: Law No. 15,352 of 25 February 2026 – amends the LGPD to establish the National Data Protection Agency (ANPD), creates the data protection regulation career and sets the commencement of the Digital Statute of Children and Adolescents (conversion of Provisional Measure No. 1,317/2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned 25 February 2026 as the conversion of Medida Provisória nº 1.317, de 17 de setembro de 2025, and published in the DOU of 25 February 2026; it also revokes Medida Provisória nº 1.319/2025. It inserts art. 41-A into Lei nº 15.211/2025 fixing that law's entry into force on 17 March 2026. Art. 20 revokes MP 1.319/2025; art. 21 provides entry into force on publication.
instruments.summary: Rewrites the LGPD's chapter on the authority so that art. 55-A creates the Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD), a special-nature autarchy linked to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security with functional, technical, decision-making, administrative and financial autonomy, and adds internal bodies such as an Auditoria. It creates the federal Carreira de Regulação e Fiscalização de Proteção de Dados and sets 17 March 2026 as the commencement date of the Digital Statute of Children and Adolescents (Lei nº 15.211/2025).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Restructures the authority (now the Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados) that enforces LGPD art. 20 and, under Decreto nº 12.622/2025, the ECA Digital, and that PL 6.237/2025 would make the central AI regulator.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 15.123, de 24 de abril de 2025
instruments.english_title: Law No. 15,123 of 24 April 2025 – amends art. 147-B of the Penal Code to increase the penalty for psychological violence against women committed using artificial intelligence or other technology that alters the victim's image or voice
instruments.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned 24 April 2025 and published in the DOU of 25 April 2025; art. 3 provides entry into force on publication.
instruments.summary: Adds a sole paragraph to art. 147-B of the Penal Code (crime of psychological violence against women) providing that the penalty is increased by half when the crime is committed using artificial intelligence or any other technological resource that alters the victim's image or sound. It applies to anyone prosecuted for the offence and is one of the first federal statutes to name artificial intelligence expressly.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Criminal-law aggravating circumstance for AI-generated or AI-altered image or voice (deepfakes) used in psychological violence against women.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 15.211, de 17 de setembro de 2025
instruments.english_title: Law No. 15,211 of 17 September 2025 – Digital Statute of Children and Adolescents (ECA Digital), on the protection of children and adolescents in digital environments
instruments.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned 17 September 2025 and published in the DOU of 17 September 2025 (extra edition). Art. 41-A, inserted first by Medida Provisória nº 1.319/2025 (six months after publication) and then by Lei nº 15.352/2026, fixes entry into force on 17 March 2026. Regulated by Decreto nº 12.622/2025 (designating the Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados as the autonomous administrative authority under the law) and Decreto nº 12.880/2026.
instruments.summary: Applies to every IT product or service directed at, or likely to be accessed by, children and adolescents in Brazil, wherever the provider is located, imposing duties on age assurance, protective default settings, parental supervision, content and contact risks, advertising and legal representation in Brazil, enforced by an autonomous administrative authority. Among the default parental-supervision settings it requires control over personalised recommendation systems (including the option to turn them off) and regular review of artificial intelligence tools, with experts and competent bodies, against technical criteria ensuring their safety for children, with the option to disable non-essential functions; art. 22 bans profiling and emotional analysis for targeting commercial advertising at children and adolescents.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding duties on recommender systems, profiling and AI tools in digital services used by minors.

instruments.official_title: Decreto nº 12.880, de 18 de março de 2026
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 12,880 of 18 March 2026 – regulates the Digital Statute of Children and Adolescents (Law No. 15,211/2025) and establishes the National Policy for the Promotion and Protection of the Rights of Children and Adolescents in the Digital Environment
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidência da República
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Signed 18 March 2026 and published in the DOU of 18 March 2026 (extra edition); art. 54 provides entry into force on publication.
instruments.summary: Regulates Lei nº 15.211/2025 and establishes a national policy on children's rights in the digital environment. Art. 11 requires providers of services directed at or likely to be accessed by children that generate content and interact from natural-language instructions (including language models and conversational agents) to be transparent about their synthetic and automated character, prevent behavioural manipulation, assess algorithmic risk to children's safety and health and implement safeguards, with the ANPD to regulate and supervise; it also treats artificial or automated systems producing sexually explicit dialogue, images or video as pornographic content subject to age-verification duties.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First federal regulation with express obligations for generative AI and conversational agents (transparency, anti-manipulation, algorithmic risk assessment) where children are users.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 15.487, de 6 de agosto de 2026
instruments.english_title: Law No. 15,487 of 6 August 2026 – measures to combat and punish sexual violence against children and adolescents, including in the digital environment and using artificial intelligence (amends the Penal Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, ECA, Heinous Crimes Law and Organised Crime Law)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned 6 August 2026 (from PL 3.066/2025) and published in the DOU of 7 August 2026; art. 7 provides entry into force on publication.
instruments.summary: Toughens criminal law on sexual violence against children and adolescents. It rewrites ECA art. 241-C to criminalise simulating a child's participation in sexual-violence content by altering or manipulating images or video, including with artificial intelligence (3-5 years' imprisonment), defines child sexual-violence material in new art. 241-E to cover real or fictitious depictions produced, manipulated or generated with digital technologies including AI, and increases grooming penalties by one third to two thirds when the offender uses AI, deepfakes or filters to pose as a child.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Criminalises AI-generated and deepfake child sexual-abuse material and AI-assisted grooming.

instruments.official_title: Decreto nº 12.976, de 20 de maio de 2026
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 12,976 of 20 May 2026 – guidelines for the protection of women on the internet and for combating violence against women in the digital environment
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidência da República
instruments.publisher_name: Presidência da República (Casa Civil, Secretaria Especial para Assuntos Jurídicos)
instruments.current_status: Signed 20 May 2026 (under Lei nº 12.965/2014, the Marco Civil da Internet) and published in the DOU of 21 May 2026. Art. 15: in force sixty days after publication; 20 July 2026 is computed from that rule (counting under Lei Complementar nº 95/1998, art. 8 § 1) and is not written in the text. Issued the same day as Decreto nº 12.975/2026, which amends Decreto nº 8.771/2016 (art. 19-A, the ANPD's competence referred to in art. 14) and has no AI wording.
instruments.summary: Sets duties for internet application providers that host third-party content to protect women: liability for systemic failure to take down crimes against women, a notice-and-takedown procedure with Ligue 180 notices, priority handling for political violence and evidence preservation, with regulation and enforcement by the Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD). Chapter III (arts. 9-10) prohibits providers from generating or modifying intimate content of third parties using artificial intelligence or any technology that alters the victim's image or voice, and requires AI-based providers to implement technical and procedural safeguards to identify and block requests to generate such content, as regulated by the competent authority; art. 3 defines intimate content to include material produced or manipulated wholly or partly by AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding prohibition on AI generation of non-consensual intimate imagery by internet providers and duty for generative-AI services to block such prompts.

instruments.official_title: Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial (PBIA) 2024-2028 — IA para o Bem de Todos
instruments.english_title: Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan (PBIA) 2024-2028 — AI for the Good of All
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (prepared with the Conselho Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia – CCT)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação
instruments.current_status: MCTI states the plan was launched during the 5ª Conferência Nacional de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação; the official page does not give the day. The CCT minutes of its 23 July 2024 ordinary meeting record the presentation of the last version of the proposal (five axes, governance and monitoring structure). No presidential decree formally approving the plan was found in the DOU or on planalto.gov.br. Its management is operationalised by the GT-PBIA instituted by Resolução CITDigital nº 2/2025, and federal digital-government initiatives (Portaria SGD/MGI nº 6.618/2024) are framed 'no âmbito do PBIA'. The full plan document is published through the CGEE platform linked from the MCTI page (pbia.cgee.org.br, a script-only application) and could not be read; facts here come from the MCTI page and the CCT minutes.
instruments.scope: Federal government; national AI investment and policy plan
instruments.summary: Federal AI plan for 2024-2028 coordinated by MCTI, combining immediate-impact actions with structural actions in five axes: AI infrastructure and development; diffusion, training and capacity building; AI to improve public services; AI for business innovation; and support for the AI regulatory and governance process. Its stated objectives include high-performance computing powered by renewable energy, Portuguese-language large language models built on national data, large-scale training and re-skilling, and a global role for Brazil in AI, with investment of about R$ 23 billion over four years. The CCT proposal described a governance and monitoring structure and a Brazilian AI Observatory (OBIA).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Brazilian federal instrument shaping AI governance (strategy, government-governance, public-sector).

instruments.issuing_authority: Secretaria de Governo Digital do Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos

Under Objective 6 (smart use of data) it fixes AI initiatives framed under the Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial: an AI development and deployment platform for the federal executive, a nucleus for structuring and experimenting AI projects, good practices on AI governance, risk assessment and ethics, guidance, standards and models for AI adoption in ten priority areas, and an annual survey of AI adoption.

instruments.issuing_authority: Secretaria de Governo Digital do Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos
instruments.publisher_name: Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos

New AI-related recommendations call for risk-proportionate governance of public-sector AI with defined responsibilities, oversight bodies and impact self-assessment; adoption of AI assistants, agents and automation; guides, standards and reference models for procuring, developing and using AI; mapping AI use cases with ethical safeguards; transparency on the purpose, functioning and impacts of AI solutions proportional to risk; and AI literacy programmes for public servants.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Brazilian federal instrument shaping AI governance (strategy, public-sector, transparency).

instruments.english_title: MGI Ordinance No. 3,485 of 24 April 2026 — Artificial Intelligence Governance Policy of the Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos (Minister, substitute)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos

Cites Resolução CGDSI/MGI nº 10/2025 (E-IA/MGI) and Portaria MCTI nº 4.617/2021 (EBIA) as bases; Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): DOU entry header: 'Publicado em: 28/04/2026 | Edição: 78 | Seção: 1 | Página: 70'. instruments.summary: Establishes principles, guidelines and responsibilities for developing, acquiring and using AI applications at MGI, with principles including human rights, transparency, security, privacy, human oversight and accountability, sustainability and digital sovereignty. It sets a governance structure (senior management, the digital governance committee CGDSI, an AI subcommittee, IT, data, privacy and internal-control officers), requires risk-proportionate human oversight, incident notification and explicit disclosure when AI is used in products or documents. Use of public generative-AI platforms is limited to public information, barring confidential and personal data unless a prior risk assessment authorises it, and a continuous AI training programme is created.

instruments.current_status: Version 1, dated Brasília, 1 September 2022; announced on the ANVISA news page of 19 October 2022. Later versions not checked.
instruments.summary: ANVISA's official answers to questions received on RDC nº 657/2022, classifying many concrete software products and explaining notification and registration routes. For software that uses artificial intelligence to achieve or support its medical purpose, it states that companies must submit a report justifying the AI technique used, the size of the datasets, the training history, and a description of the data used for learning, training and verification (origin, quantity, description) with statistical justification of dataset size. AI-based products may be treated as innovative technology requiring clinical analysis.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Brazilian federal regulator instrument shaping AI governance (sectoral, risk-assurance).

instruments.official_title: Resolução Anatel nº 777, de 28 de abril de 2025
instruments.english_title: Anatel Resolution No. 777 of 28 April 2025 approving the General Regulation of Telecommunications Services (RGST), including AI principles

instruments.summary: Approves the General Regulation of Telecommunications Services and revokes or amends dozens of earlier Anatel resolutions. Art. 40 of the Regulation requires telecom licensees using AI-based solutions to observe, besides existing law, eight principles: reliability; fairness and accountability; non-discrimination; plurality; privacy and data protection; respect for fundamental rights and democratic values; sustainability; and transparency and explainability. Breach of these principles may lead to corrective measures and sanctions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Brazilian federal regulator instrument shaping AI governance (sectoral, ethics).

instruments.official_title: Decreto nº 67.799, de 13 de julho de 2023
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 67,799 of 13 July 2023 instituting the Digital Government Strategy 2023-2026 of the State of São Paulo
instruments.issuing_authority: Governo do Estado de São Paulo
instruments.publisher_name: Governo do Estado de São Paulo
instruments.current_status: Signed 13 July 2023, published in the Diário Oficial do Estado (DOE-I) 14 July 2023, p. 1; in force on publication (art. 12). Amended by Decreto nº 68.312/2024 (art. 12 revocations only); ALESP lists it as 'sem revogação expressa'. Covers the period 2023-2026.
instruments.summary: Gubernatorial decree establishing São Paulo's Digital Government Strategy for 2023-2026 for the direct and autarchic state administration. Its principles include 'automation through investment in technology and artificial intelligence' and one of its objectives is to 'encourage the use of artificial intelligence in implementing public policies'; each body must adopt an ICT master plan (PDTIC) submitted to the state ICT council (COETIC), with the Secretaria de Gestão e Governo Digital coordinating implementation and PRODESP providing services.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: São Paulo's state-level digital government strategy, which sets AI adoption as a principle and objective for the state administration.

instruments.official_title: Decreto nº 68.828, de 4 de setembro de 2024
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 68,828 of 4 September 2024 instituting the Muralha Paulista Programme (State of São Paulo)
instruments.issuing_authority: Governo do Estado de São Paulo
instruments.publisher_name: Governo do Estado de São Paulo
instruments.current_status: Signed 4 September 2024, published in the DOE-SP Executivo Seção 1 on 5 September 2024, p. 9; in force on publication (art. 19), revoking Decreto nº 60.761/2014. ALESP indexes it under the keyword 'Inteligência Artificial'; no express revocation recorded.
instruments.summary: Creates the Muralha Paulista programme of the Secretaria da Segurança Pública, defined as an integrated set of physical infrastructure, cloud and artificial-intelligence solutions that pools audiovisual and georeferencing sensor data from state bodies, municipalities, concessionaires and voluntary private collaborators to track 'criminal mobility'. It provides for analysis 'including with the use of artificial intelligence, supported by human curation', restricts the products to public-security purposes, commits to LGPD compliance and requires the Secretariat to set data-security protocols, audit reports on system use, data governance and an access-governance commission.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding state rules for a large AI-enabled public-security surveillance and analytics programme, including human curation, purpose limitation and audit requirements.

instruments.official_title: Resolução Unesp nº 13, de 22 de abril de 2025
instruments.english_title: Unesp Resolution No. 13 of 22 April 2025 on the use of artificial intelligence at São Paulo State University
instruments.issuing_authority: Universidade Estadual Paulista "Júlio de Mesquita Filho"
instruments.publisher_name: Universidade Estadual Paulista "Júlio de Mesquita Filho"
instruments.current_status: Issued by the Rector on 22 April 2025 following Deliberação nº 04/2025 of the competent collegiate bodies (18 February 2025); published in the DOE-SP (Executivo, Atos Normativos, Universidade Estadual Paulista) on 16 May 2025; in force on publication (art. 11).
instruments.summary: Internal regulation of the state university Unesp setting principles (ethics, academic honesty, user responsibility, fairness and non-discrimination, 'human sovereignty'), guidelines and procedures for any use of AI systems in teaching, research, extension, administration and innovation. It requires human supervision and validation of all AI outputs, public disclosure of AI use that significantly affects authorship (non-disclosure may be treated as plagiarism) and LGPD compliance, and obliges Unesp to set up an AI governance structure, area-specific conduct guides, training and an ombudsman complaints channel, with the CSTI resolving omissions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding AI-use policy of a São Paulo state university (autarchy of the state administration).

instruments.official_title: Deliberação Consu-A-05/2026, de 31 de março de 2026
instruments.english_title: University Council Deliberation Consu-A-05/2026 of 31 March 2026 on the use of generative artificial intelligence at Unicamp
instruments.issuing_authority: Universidade Estadual de Campinas
instruments.publisher_name: Universidade Estadual de Campinas
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Conselho Universitário at its 195th ordinary session on 31 March 2026; published in the DOE-SP (Executivo, Universidade Estadual de Campinas) on 14 April 2026; in force on publication (art. 9). Art. 7 asks Crefia/Detic to propose specific regulation within six months, to be approved by Rector's resolution.
instruments.summary: Sets the policy for use of generative AI at the State University of Campinas by teaching and administrative staff, students, volunteers and programme participants, excluding methodological use of AI techniques in research. It establishes principles (human creativity and authorship, accuracy, transparency, user accountability for generated content, LGPD protection of personal and confidential data, attention to algorithmic bias) and guidelines that generative AI be an auxiliary tool and that the main intellectual contribution remain human, with the Centro de Referência em Tecnologias de IA (Crefia/Detic) monitoring adoption and preparing detailed rules.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding generative-AI use policy of a São Paulo state university.

instruments.official_title: Deliberação da Mesa nº 2.873, de 11 de agosto de 2025

instruments.publisher_name: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado de Minas Gerais
instruments.current_status: Signed by the Mesa on 11 August 2025; published in the Diário Administrativo da ALMG on 19 August 2025, p. 1; in force on publication (art. 6). Art. 5 (committee composition) amended by Deliberação da Mesa nº 2.886/2026 (Diário Administrativo 30 May 2026), renaming the DPC as the Diretoria de Tecnologia da Informação.
instruments.summary: Institutes the Política de Uso Responsável de Inteligência Artificial of the Minas Gerais Legislative Assembly, grounded in the Marco Civil da Internet, the LGPD and the Assembly's integrity and information-security policies. It sets nine principles (alignment, transparency, oversight, proportionality, equity, reliability, privacy, security, socio-environmental responsibility), and guidelines requiring staff training, public identification of AI-based processes, auditability of AI solutions and continuous monitoring with impact and risk assessments. It creates a Comitê Gestor da Política de IA to monitor implementation, vet AI tools, manage AI risks and propose standards.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI governance policy binding on the Minas Gerais state legislature's own use of AI.

instruments.official_title: Resolução Conjunta PGJ CGMP nº 6, de 4 de junho de 2025
instruments.english_title: Joint Resolution PGJ CGMP No. 6 of 4 June 2025 on the Policy for the Development, Implementation and Safe and Responsible Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Public Prosecutor's Office of Minas Gerais
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministério Público do Estado de Minas Gerais
instruments.publisher_name: Ministério Público do Estado de Minas Gerais
instruments.current_status: Signed in Belo Horizonte on 4 June 2025 by the Procurador-Geral de Justiça and the Corregedor-Geral; published in the Diário Oficial Eletrônico do MPMG on 5 June 2025; in force on publication (art. 9). Text read from the MPMG normative repository (mpnormas.mpmg.mp.br), which captures the official gazette text.
instruments.summary: Institutes the MPMG policy on developing, implementing and using generative AI, binding members, staff, interns, outsourced and accredited service providers. Users remain fully responsible and human supervision of AI-assisted acts is non-transferable; principles include human-centricity, non-discrimination, effective human oversight, risk management, data protection, transparency and accountability. Guidelines favour tools that keep shared data confidential, bar sharing non-anonymised personal data with tools that retrain on inputs, require confidentiality undertakings in AI contracts, bias monitoring and usage logs for traceability, with the IT Strategy Committee (CETI) responsible for governance and training.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding generative-AI governance policy of a state public prosecutor's office.

instruments.official_title: Portaria Conjunta nº 1834/PR/2026
instruments.english_title: Joint Ordinance No. 1834/PR/2026 of the Court of Justice of Minas Gerais instituting the Artificial Intelligence Committee and guidelines for prioritising AI solutions
instruments.issuing_authority: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado de Minas Gerais
instruments.publisher_name: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado de Minas Gerais
instruments.current_status: Signed 23 July 2026 by the TJMG President, Vice-Presidents and Corregedor-Geral; DJe 27 July 2026, publication 28 July 2026; in force on publication with retroactive effect from 1 July 2026 (art. 5). Implements CNJ Resolução nº 615/2025 at the TJMG. An earlier Portaria Conjunta nº 1776/PR/2026 (DJe 20 February 2026) instituted an AI business and governance executive group.
instruments.summary: Creates the TJMG Artificial Intelligence Committee to coordinate and supervise AI use and development in the court, approve proposals to use, develop or procure AI solutions, adopt AI governance policies and procedures, order audits, ensure training, and keep every AI development auditable with full lifecycle records in line with CNJ Resolution 615/2025 and the LGPD. It sets prioritisation criteria for new AI functionalities, including information security, impact on adjudication, data protection, fundamental rights and non-discrimination, and transparency, explainability, auditability and accountability.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: State court AI governance instrument implementing the national judiciary AI rules (CNJ Res. 615/2025) in Minas Gerais.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 22.324, de 2 de abril de 2025
instruments.english_title: Law No. 22,324 of 2 April 2025 instituting the Artificial Intelligence Guidelines Plan for the State Public Administration (PDIA/PR) and amending the laws it specifies (Paraná)
instruments.issuing_authority: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Paraná
instruments.publisher_name: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Paraná
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned by Governor Carlos Massa Ratinho Junior on 2 April 2025 (bill PL 528/2024) and published in the Diário Oficial do Estado nº 11876 of 2 April 2025; in force on publication (art. 19). The collegiate body it provides for was regulated by Decreto nº 9.854/2025 (Conselho Estadual de Inteligência Artificial). Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Legislação PR entry: 'Lei 22.324 - 2 de Abril de 2025 / Publicado no Diário Oficial nº. 11876 de 2 de Abril de 2025'. Effective date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Art. 19: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor na data de sua publicação' + DOE nº 11876 of 2 April 2025 (Legislação PR entry).
instruments.summary: Institutes the Plano de Diretrizes de Inteligência Artificial na Administração Pública Estadual (PDIA/PR), set out in Annex I, to promote ethical, transparent and efficient development and use of AI in Paraná's executive branch, and renames the innovation secretariat the Secretaria de Estado da Inovação e Inteligência Artificial (SEIA) with new duties to develop policies for ethical and responsible AI adoption and an innovation-friendly AI regulatory environment. A collegiate body chaired by SEIA must monitor AI projects, broker private-sector partnerships and proofs of concept, ensure transparency of AI operations with regular reports, and run continuous training for public servants. The annexed plan covers AI ethics, responsible AI, accountability, an AI regulatory sandbox for public administration and a risk matrix.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Paraná's statutory AI plan for the state administration and the legal basis of its AI secretariat and AI council.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 22.343, de 4 de abril de 2025
instruments.english_title: Law No. 22,343 of 4 April 2025 on the regulation of the use of artificial intelligence in the State of Paraná
instruments.issuing_authority: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Paraná
instruments.publisher_name: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Paraná
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned 4 April 2025 (parliamentary bill, Dep. Requião Filho) and published in the Diário Oficial do Estado nº 11878 of 4 April 2025; in force on publication (art. 7). Cited as a basis by Decreto nº 9.854/2025.
instruments.summary: Short framework law on the use of AI in the State of Paraná, defining AI as a digital system's capacity to perform tasks commonly associated with human intelligence. It sets principles of transparency and explainability, responsibility, privacy and data protection, accessibility and non-discrimination with a human-centred approach, allows the state to adopt strategies with clear procedures for evaluating, accepting, monitoring and controlling AI solutions, and prohibits using AI to invade the privacy of public servants and citizens or in investigations not authorised by a court. The executive must ensure AI use is transparent, explainable and accountable.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Paraná's general state law on AI use, including a prohibition on privacy-invasive and unauthorised investigative uses.

instruments.english_title: Decree No. 9,854 of 7 May 2025 regulating the State Artificial Intelligence Council (COIA) referred to in Law 22,324/2025 (Paraná)
instruments.issuing_authority: Governo do Estado do Paraná
instruments.publisher_name: Governo do Estado do Paraná

instruments.summary: Creates the Conselho Estadual de Inteligência Artificial (COIA), a consultative, normative and deliberative body of the Paraná executive chaired by the Secretary of Innovation and AI with the Casa Civil, PGE, SEAP, SEFA, SEPL and SETI. As amended in 2026, it monitors public AI projects against the IA.PR strategy, approves technical protocols ensuring transparency of state AI operations, sets guidelines for assessing social and economic impact (originally also algorithmic-bias and discrimination risk), proposes policies protecting personal data and citizens' rights in AI systems, sets data-governance guidelines for AI, and promotes open-source, shared model repositories and social participation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of Paraná's state AI governance council.

instruments.official_title: Lei nº 19.450, de 5 de setembro de 2025
instruments.english_title: Law No. 19,450 of 5 September 2025 on principles and guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence in the State Public Administration (Santa Catarina)
instruments.issuing_authority: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado de Santa Catarina
instruments.publisher_name: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado de Santa Catarina
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned by Governor Jorginho Mello on 5 September 2025 (PL 0049/2024, Dep. instruments.summary: Sets principles and guidelines for the responsible use of AI by the direct and indirect state administration of Santa Catarina (it does not apply to private actors). It lists principles including effective human oversight, non-discrimination, transparency, explainability and auditability, due process and contestability, traceability, accountability and risk prevention, and grants people affected by state AI systems rights to prior information, explanation, contestation of decisions with legal or significant effects, human participation, correction of discriminatory bias and data protection. The administration must periodically evaluate AI systems in operation and issue guidance on transparent and ethical use, and the executive may authorise an experimental regulatory environment (sandbox) for AI innovation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Santa Catarina's state AI law for the public administration, with rights for affected persons modelled on the federal AI bill.

instruments.official_title: Decreto nº 1.609, de 10 de julho de 2026
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 1,609 of 10 July 2026 regulating Law 19,450/2025 and instituting the State Policy for the Design, Use and Governance of Artificial Intelligence Solutions of the Executive Branch (PEIA) (Santa Catarina)
instruments.issuing_authority: Governo do Estado de Santa Catarina
instruments.publisher_name: Governo do Estado de Santa Catarina
instruments.current_status: Signed 10 July 2026 by Governor Jorginho Mello; in force on publication (art. 39). The ALESC portal lists its validity from 10 July 2026 ('Vigência 10/07/2026 - atual'); the DOE-SC edition number was not shown, so the publication date is taken from that validity date.
instruments.summary: Regulates Lei 19.450/2025 by creating the PEIA, a three-tier AI governance structure for the Santa Catarina executive: a Central AI Committee (CCIA/SC) under the Science, Technology and Innovation Secretariat that can adopt, restrict or suspend high-risk AI systems and sets risk-classification and impact-assessment criteria, a Technical AI Committee keeping a state catalogue of AI systems, and sectoral AI units in each body. It defines high-risk AI (affecting fundamental rights, sensitive data, automated triage for access to rights or benefits, high-gravity decisions), requires a prior Algorithmic Impact Assessment (AIA) and continuous monitoring for such systems, obliges bodies to explain automated decisions, keep a human channel and allow review by a public agent, and requires prior review for use of sensitive personal data. It mandates AI-specific contract clauses (governance, security, data protection, ownership of trained models), bars suppliers from using state data to train their own models without authorisation, creates a public State AI Portal and the Sandbox Regulatório Catarinense de IA.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Comprehensive state-level AI governance regulation with risk classification, algorithmic impact assessment, procurement clauses and a regulatory sandbox.

instruments.official_title: Decreto nº 1.642, de 5 de agosto de 2026
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 1,642 of 5 August 2026 instituting the Integrated Intelligent Video-Monitoring System of Santa Catarina (SIVI-SC) within the Public Security Secretariat
instruments.issuing_authority: Governo do Estado de Santa Catarina
instruments.publisher_name: Governo do Estado de Santa Catarina

instruments.summary: Creates SIVI-SC, the state public-security video-monitoring system using image analytics, facial recognition and AI (including automated plate reading, anomaly and crowd detection and automated disaster alerts), coordinated by the Secretaria de Estado da Segurança Pública. Automated alerts are only supportive and do not replace validation by the competent agent; it prohibits monitoring private spaces without legal or judicial authorisation, parameterising analyses on discriminatory attributes or sensitive data, and indiscriminate use, and sets LGPD-based data minimisation, access control with multifactor authentication, five-year audit logs and data-sharing rules. Facial recognition must observe Lei 19.450/2025, and user bodies must adopt internal rules including a minimum 85% accuracy threshold for triggering alerts.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding state rules for AI-based facial recognition and video analytics in public security, with prohibited uses and an accuracy threshold.

instruments.issuing_authority: Secretaria de Planejamento, Governança e Gestão do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul
instruments.publisher_name: Secretaria de Planejamento, Governança e Gestão do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul
instruments.current_status: Signed in Porto Alegre on 8 April 2026 by the Secretary of Planning, Governance and Management under Decreto nº 57.547/2024 (state ICT policy); published in the Diário Oficial do Estado on 14 April 2026; in force on publication (art. 4). instruments.summary: Adopts, as its single annex, the AI Strategy of the Rio Grande do Sul state administration for 2026-2027, applicable to all direct and indirect administration bodies. It sets principles (trust, transparency and security; inclusion; sustainability; human oversight with full human responsibility; data protection) and guidelines requiring explainable and auditable algorithms with decision logs, citizens' right to contest and review automated decisions and to be told the degree of automation, human review before AI-generated information is released, bias testing of datasets, and formal approval by the central ICT body of any third-party AI solution. Six objectives (smart services via the GurIA assistant, an AI governance and risk model, transparency and explainability, technology architecture, innovation including sandboxes, and AI skills) come with indicators, 2026-2027 targets and assigned actions, such as an ethical and risk assessment model for AI projects and an AI repository in the state data platform.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Rio Grande do Sul's state AI strategy for the public administration, issued as a binding normative instruction.

instruments.official_title: Lei Complementar nº 205, de 19 de maio de 2025
instruments.english_title: Complementary Law No. 205 of 19 May 2025 instituting the State Policy for Promoting Innovation in Artificial Intelligence in the State of Goiás
instruments.issuing_authority: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado de Goiás
instruments.publisher_name: Assembleia Legislativa do Estado de Goiás
instruments.current_status: Sanctioned by Governor Ronaldo Caiado on 19 May 2025 (governor's bill, process 2025011324) and published in the Suplemento of the Diário Oficial do Estado of 19 May 2025; in force on publication (art. 79). Amended by Lei Complementar nº 215 of 10 September 2026 (D.O. supplement of 10 September 2026), which moves the NEI-IA ethics unit and the state computing centre under the Secretaria de Estado de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (SECTI) and gives FAPEG the funding role. instruments.summary: Comprehensive state AI law of Goiás (ementa: Política Estadual de Fomento à Inovação em Inteligência Artificial) with an innovation-first approach: it declares private development and use of AI for lawful purposes free, bars presumptions of risk against lawful technologies under development, limits algorithmic audits to strictly necessary cases, and gives a preference to open-source AI in public projects. It grants rights to non-discrimination and to prior, accessible information when AI is used for automated decisions (with information on the decision premises when access to rights is affected), prohibits AI uses contrary to fundamental rights or democratic order, and sets objectives for AI in public services. instruments.scope: Direct and indirect administration of the Belo Horizonte Executive
instruments.summary: Establishes Belo Horizonte's Data Intelligence Policy, with principles of transparency, evidence-based decisions, data integrity and ethical data treatment, and a data-governance model (life-cycle management under the LGPD, interoperability, access control, metadata, monitoring). It makes the municipal IT company Prodabel the policy manager, tasked with a data platform offering advanced analytics including machine learning and artificial intelligence. Article 9 requires any use of AI resources to respect individual and collective rights, prevent discriminatory bias and ensure transparency so citizens can understand the decision criteria adopted with AI, and defines AI.

instruments.scope: Public agents of the Procuradoria-Geral do Município de Porto Alegre
instruments.summary: Sets guidelines for AI use, especially generative AI, by public agents of Porto Alegre's Municipal Attorney-General's Office. Use must comply with the PGM organic law, the municipal staff statute, the LGPD and the Civil Procedure Code, protect confidential and restricted data, be ethical and responsible with constant human supervision, and rely on secure sources for doctrine and case law. All AI outputs must be reviewed for accuracy and bias, users remain solely responsible for AI-assisted content, and AI may only support, never replace, human analysis and decisions.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 in five parts (B1 federal law and bills; B2 federal government; B3 federal regulators; B4 states; B5 cities). No usage-limit interruption occurred; every record was built from official texts read in this run and the three earlier records were re-checked and fixed (site-name suffixes removed, domain-named publisher replaced). Second fetch method (BACKFILL step 4) was used throughout: Planalto and MCTI pages refused Chrome-agent curl and WebFetch but loaded with a Firefox user agent; several state portals were read via WebFetch. index-readiness: no government-published AI readiness index found. Located-only (4): TSE Resoluções 23.732/2024 and 23.755/2026 (tse.jus.br, all TRE sites, sintse and DJE returned 403 to curl with Chrome and Firefox agents and to WebFetch); PBIA 2024-2028 (full text only on the JavaScript-only pbia.cgee.org.br; MCTI page and CCT minutes of 23 July 2024 read; no approving decree or CCT resolution found); Rio Lei 8.926/2025 (Câmara Municipal legislation site unreachable; content from the Prefeitura's report and the D.O. Rio veto message). Decreto 12.976/2026 was found by the lead's own check of a decree cited in B3 leads (AI appears only in the body text, not the index summary); Decreto 12.975/2026 has no AI wording. LGPD effective date 2020-09-18 follows Lei 14.058/2020 (conversion of MP 959/2020 without the deferral). ANPD organisation recorded under its current name (Lei 15.352/2026); earlier documents keep 'Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados' as issuing authority. AI-enabled public-security decrees (São Paulo Smart Sampa, SP Muralha Paulista, SC SIVI-SC) are recorded as sectoral; Smart Sampa's decree does not use the words 'inteligência artificial'. Salvador and Fortaleza: web searches only, nothing found. cyber-security: no AI-specific guidance from the GSI or CTIR Gov was found (lead-level web search; gov.br/gsi not searched in depth). standards: ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 42001:2024 and 23894:2023 appear in commercial standards catalogues but were not confirmed on ABNT's official catalogue, so they are held as a lead. international: the G20 Maceió (2024) and BRICS Rio (2025) AI texts were not found on a Brazilian government site and are leads.

leads.issuing_authority: Congresso Nacional (Senado Federal; Câmara dos Deputados)
leads.note: Introduced in the Senate by Sen. Rodrigo Pacheco on 3 May 2023. Senate plenary approved it on 10 December 2024 in the form of the substitute (Emenda nº 199) of the Comissão Temporária Interna sobre Inteligência Artificial, rapporteur Sen. Eduardo Gomes (Parecer nº 207/2024-PLEN); the substitute was definitively adopted in the supplementary round the same day and PLs 5.051/2019, 5.691/2019, 21/2020, 872/2021, 3.592/2023, 210/2024 and 266/2024 were declared prejudicados. Sent to the Câmara by Ofício SF nº 235 on 17 March 2025 (presented there 17 March 2025). Câmara: special committee created 4 April 2025 and constituted 29 April 2025; rapporteur Dep. Aguinaldo Ribeiro (PP-PB) designated 20 May 2025; priority regime, subject to Plenary. Government bill PL 6.237/2025 and many other AI bills attached (apensados). Status on 11 October 2026: 'Aguardando Parecer' in the special committee (last movement 2 September 2026); no committee report or vote recorded; not enacted. Senate: https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/atividade/materias/-/materia/157233 ; Câmara: https://www.camara.leg.br/proposicoesWeb/fichadetramitacao?idProposicao=2487262
